Definition: Approved start date for the project control baseline.
Approved planned end date for the project.
Cut-off date for reported progress, actual costs, and EVM metrics.
Hierarchical breakdown of project scope into controllable work packages or activities.
Unique identifier used to connect WBS activities to baseline PV, actual costs, and progress facts.
A controllable unit of project work with budget, schedule, progress, and cost tracking.
Planned start date for a WBS activity from the approved baseline.
Planned finish date for a WBS activity from the approved baseline.
Calendar-day span between baseline start and finish dates.
Timeline chart showing planned activity timing and duration by WBS activity.
Approved total budget for the project or WBS activity.
Budgeted value of work planned to be complete by a given date.
Actual cost incurred by a given date.
Latest reported percent complete for each WBS activity as of the status date.
Budgeted value of the work actually completed; calculated as BAC × progress.
EV minus PV; negative means less work completed than planned.
EV minus AC; negative means cost overrun for completed work.
EV divided by PV; below 1.0 indicates unfavorable schedule efficiency.
EV divided by AC; below 1.0 indicates unfavorable cost efficiency.
Forecast final project or WBS cost, typically BAC divided by CPI.
Forecast remaining cost to complete the work; EAC minus AC.
Expected budget variance at completion; BAC minus EAC.
Line chart comparing cumulative PV, EV, and AC over time.
Good condition: on/above plan, favorable variance, or acceptable performance threshold.
Watch condition: close to threshold or mid-progress; monitor closely.
Action condition: negative variance, low progress, CPI/SPI below threshold, or overrun.
Management summary view showing KPIs, WBS performance, trend data, and RAG status.
Validation that dashboard KPIs match the detailed EVM reporting table at the status date.
Reference table describing projects, WBS, resources, or calendar dates.
Transaction or event table containing planned values, actual costs, or progress observations.
Source data or user-entered content that feeds project calculations and reports.
Assumptions, thresholds, validation, governance, and planning logic used to interpret inputs.
Reports, charts, dashboards, and references produced from the input data and control logic.
